existing_capabilities: findings: empty_password, cred_access, local_infile, file_priv, datamine, no_tls

missing_capabilities.name: caching_sha2_password auth (MySQL 8.0 default)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: MySQL Internals — 'caching_sha2_password Information'; server_default_auth changed to caching_sha2_password in 8.0.4
missing_capabilities.description: Module only implements mysql_native_password. Against a stock MySQL 8.0 server whose default plugin is caching_sha2_password, the empty-password probe fails at AuthSwitchRequest — recce records 'auth negotiation required' and moves on, missing genuinely-empty root on 8.x. Need to (a) handle AuthSwitchRequest (0xFE), (b) implement SHA256 scramble = SHA256(pw) XOR SHA256( SHA256(SHA256(pw)) || salt ), and (c) handle fast-auth / full-auth branches (0x01 0x03 = fast success, 0x01 0x04 = perform_full_authentication).

missing_capabilities.name: AuthSwitchRequest (0xFE) plugin switching
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: MySQL Internals — Protocol::AuthSwitchRequest / AuthSwitchResponse
missing_capabilities.description: Server may respond with plugin != client-declared. Module treats any 0xFE as failure; it should read new plugin name + salt and answer with the correct scramble. Also gates sha256_password, mysql_clear_password (PAM/LDAP), ed25519 (MariaDB), dialog and mysql_old_password. Without this, all non-native servers report as 'auth required' even when empty/weak.

missing_capabilities.name: sha256_password + RSA public-key exchange
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: MySQL 5.6+ sha256_password plugin; caching_sha2_password full-auth path uses same RSA public key
missing_capabilities.description: Full-auth path over cleartext-only channel requires requesting the server's RSA pubkey (0x02) and RSA-OAEP encrypting the XOR'd password. Not implemented — blocks credentialed follow-through on hardened 8.0 hosts and any 5.7 that set default_authentication_plugin=sha256_password.

missing_capabilities.name: MariaDB ed25519 + mysql_clear_password / dialog (PAM)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: MariaDB Knowledge Base — 'Authentication Plugin - ed25519' and 'PAM Authentication Plugin'
missing_capabilities.description: MariaDB defaults to mysql_native_password but ed25519 is common. PAM/LDAP-backed accounts negotiate mysql_clear_password (client sends cleartext) or dialog — a valuable capture surface: recce could authenticate with looted cleartext creds against a PAM-backed account, and could flag servers that force cleartext over unencrypted transport (credential capture risk).

missing_capabilities.name: CVE-2012-2122 memcmp auth-bypass probe
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: CVE-2012-2122 — MariaDB/MySQL 5.1.x < 5.1.62, 5.5.x < 5.5.23, 5.6.x < 5.6.6 on affected glibc
missing_capabilities.description: 1-in-256 chance that any wrong password authenticates. A trivial 300-iteration loop of _login with a bogus scramble against `root` detects it. Legacy MariaDB in the wild still exists in air-gapped estates.

missing_capabilities.name: MySQL X Protocol (port 33060) probe
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: MySQL X Protocol (Protobuf, mysqlx port 33060; ConnPlain/MYSQL41/SHA256_MEMORY/PLAIN SASL)
missing_capabilities.description: Module claims 33060 in _PORTS but only speaks the classic protocol on it — will fail every handshake. X Protocol is protobuf-framed and offers PLAIN (cleartext creds if TLS off), MYSQL41 (native scramble) and SHA256_MEMORY. Missing: capabilities read (Mysqlx.Connection.CapabilitiesGet), SASL mech list, PLAIN over cleartext finding, native/sha256 auth. Same admin surface as 3306, often overlooked.

missing_capabilities.name: mysql.func UDF enumeration
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: MySQL Reference — CREATE FUNCTION ... SONAME; mysql.func table
missing_capabilities.description: SELECT * FROM mysql.func lists ALREADY-LOADED UDFs. Presence of lib_mysqludf_sys (sys_exec, sys_eval) is instant OS command execution as the mysql user without needing FILE priv or plugin_dir write. Currently unread.

missing_capabilities.name: Plugins / audit / keyring inventory (SHOW PLUGINS + mysql.plugin)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: MySQL Reference — INFORMATION_SCHEMA.PLUGINS, mysql.plugin
missing_capabilities.description: authentication_ldap_sasl / authentication_pam / keyring_file / audit_log / semisync configuration is scanner-visible. LDAP plugin points at the domain controller (feeds domains/hostnames). Missing audit_log = quiet exfil.

missing_capabilities.name: Replication topology enumeration
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: MySQL Reference — SHOW REPLICA STATUS / SHOW SLAVE STATUS / SHOW SLAVE HOSTS / SHOW MASTER STATUS / performance_schema.replication_connection_configuration
missing_capabilities.description: Exposes master hostname/IP, replication username, port, GTID, and downstream replica IPs. Replication user typically has REPLICATION SLAVE (readable binlog → historical writes with values). None of this is queried today. Pure XREF gold for hostnames/relay_targets.

missing_capabilities.name: information_schema.PROCESSLIST / performance_schema.threads
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: MySQL Reference — SHOW PROCESSLIST / information_schema.PROCESSLIST
missing_capabilities.description: Enumerates live client IPs, connected usernames, current SQL text (may contain literal secrets). Feeds relay_targets (which hosts actually talk to this DB) and known_users (real service accounts, not just mysql.user rows).

missing_capabilities.name: Stored procedures / functions / triggers / events with DEFINER
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: MySQL Reference — information_schema.ROUTINES / TRIGGERS / EVENTS; SQL SECURITY DEFINER semantics
missing_capabilities.description: SQL SECURITY DEFINER routines run with the definer's privs — a common privesc when a low-priv account can INVOKE a DEFINER=`root`@`%` procedure. Also mines routine bodies for embedded literals / secrets.

missing_capabilities.name: mysql.user host-wildcard and anonymous-account audit
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: MySQL Reference — GRANT syntax host wildcards; anonymous users (user='')
missing_capabilities.description: Rows like 'root'@'%' or user='' regardless of password state are a finding of their own — recce already reads the table but never flags wide-host or anonymous rows unless the account also had an empty password. Anonymous account existence is a distinct issue (implicit permission granting via anonymous match).

missing_capabilities.name: Expired / never-rotated / no-password accounts (password_expired, password_last_changed)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: MySQL 5.6+ mysql.user.password_expired; 5.7+ password_last_changed / password_lifetime
missing_capabilities.description: Accounts with authentication_string='' but plugin=mysql_native_password (or 'auth_socket') are logon-any. password_expired='N' with password_last_changed years old is stale. Not surfaced.

missing_capabilities.name: Roles / GRANT OPTION / wildcard *.* privileges audit
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: MySQL 8.0 roles — mysql.role_edges, default_roles; SHOW GRANTS ... WITH GRANT OPTION; global *.* grants
missing_capabilities.description: Currently only FILE is checked. SUPER, PROCESS, REPLICATION CLIENT, CREATE USER, GRANT OPTION on *.* are each an escalation vector (SUPER → mysqld_safe hijack pre-5.7, REPLICATION CLIENT → binlog dumps, GRANT OPTION → mint new roots). Roles graph reveals inherited privileges the direct-grant check misses.

missing_capabilities.name: Version-to-CVE correlation
missing_capabilities.description: Greeting yields exact server_version string (already parsed) but no vulndb correlation is emitted. Every other recce module ties version→CVE; mysql doesn't.

missing_capabilities.name: SSL/TLS quality when TLS IS offered
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: MySQL Reference — SSL request packet; CLIENT_SSL cap; require_secure_transport
missing_capabilities.description: Module reports only ON/OFF advertising. When ON, no STARTTLS upgrade + cert grab is performed → misses self-signed default certs (auto-generated by mysql_ssl_rsa_setup), expired certs, weak protocols (TLSv1.0/1.1), weak DHE, CN=MySQL_Server_x.y.z_Auto_Generated_Server_Certificate leak, and CN/SAN hostnames (feeds hostnames DB).

missing_capabilities.name: Binary log / relay log reads (SHOW BINARY LOGS + mysqlbinlog SQL)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: MySQL Reference — SHOW BINARY LOGS, COM_BINLOG_DUMP, binlog password leaks
missing_capabilities.description: Historical writes contain literal plaintext values including CREATE USER ... IDENTIFIED BY 'plaintext' up to 5.7, ALTER USER, and INSERT INTO users VALUES(..., 'password'). REPLICATION CLIENT + SUPER grants let recce dump binlog names; a follow-up read pulls historic credentials. Not touched.

missing_capabilities.name: FILE-privilege active proof (LOAD_FILE / INTO DUMPFILE writable plugin_dir)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: MySQL Reference — LOAD_FILE(), SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE / DUMPFILE; plugin_dir semantics
missing_capabilities.description: Finding is emitted purely from privilege inference. A read-only proof — LOAD_FILE('/etc/hostname') on Linux or '/etc/mysql/debian.cnf' (contains root creds) — moves it from theoretical to confirmed, and mysql debian.cnf leak is a common one-shot creds win. Only writable-plugin_dir check is currently textual.

missing_capabilities.name: Hashcat mode per-plugin (not always -m 300)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: hashcat — 300 mysql_native_password, 7401 mysql_$A$ / mysql sha256, 21100 auth_string caching_sha2 ("$mysql-sha2")
missing_capabilities.description: Loot emits every hash with '-m 300' regardless of plugin field it already captured. caching_sha2_password / sha256_password / ed25519 hashes need different modes; wrong mode = analyst wastes wordlist time.

missing_capabilities.name: mysql.slave_master_info / mysql.slave_relay_log_info (cleartext replication creds)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: MySQL 5.6+ — mysql.slave_master_info table (User_name, User_password columns); Oracle bulletin about plaintext credential storage
missing_capabilities.description: When master_info_repository=TABLE, replication user + PLAINTEXT password sit in mysql.slave_master_info. High-value secret; module never queries it.

cross_service_wire_gaps: mysql.user usernames should feed known_users (only hashes are emitted as Credential today; the bare username list — 'root','app','backup','replicator' — never enters the shared pool)
mysql.user Host column with concrete IPs/subnets ('root'@'10.0.0.5', 'app'@'10.0.0.%') should populate relay_targets and hostnames (identifies who is trusted to talk to this DB)
@@hostname / @@report_host and replication master host from SHOW REPLICA STATUS should feed hostnames
@@version_compile_os ('Linux','Win64') already retrieved into loot['os'] but never propagated to Host.os / OS fingerprint
SHOW SLAVE HOSTS / performance_schema.replication_connection_status downstream replicas → hosts + relay_targets
information_schema.PROCESSLIST client Host column → live client IPs → relay_targets/hostnames
authentication_ldap_sasl / authentication_pam server params → domains + DC hostnames
mysql.slave_master_info replication creds → Credential(kind=password) + relay_target (the master IP)
Harvested connection strings are enrolled as Credential but the HOST part is not exploded into hostnames/relay_targets
Hash Credential.notes always says '-m 300' — should carry per-plugin hashcat mode (7401 / 21100 / MariaDB ed25519)
priority_gaps: caching_sha2_password + AuthSwitchRequest handling — without it, recce is blind against MySQL 8.0 default auth (blocks every downstream loot/datamine on 8.x)
mysql.func UDF enumeration — one SELECT reveals pre-loaded UDFs (sys_exec/sys_eval) that grant instant RCE without any FILE-priv chain
Replication + PROCESSLIST + mysql.slave_master_info — pulls plaintext replication creds, master host, and live client IPs; feeds hostnames/relay_targets/known_users across the entire engagement
Version→CVE correlation on the already-parsed server_version — CVE-2012-2122, CVE-2016-6662, CVE-2021-2154, ed25519 downgrades — every other recce service module does this and mysql doesn't
notes: Reviewed recce/services/db/mysql.py against MySQL Internals Manual, MySQL 8.0 Reference (auth plugins, replication, X Protocol), MariaDB KB (ed25519, PAM), and the mysql-specific CVE history. Module is solid on the classic-protocol empty-password + native-scramble surface but stops at MySQL 5.7-era assumptions: it does not follow AuthSwitchRequest, does not speak caching_sha2_password (8.0 default) or sha256_password / RSA, ignores X Protocol on 33060 despite claiming the port, never enumerates replication topology / PROCESSLIST / mysql.func / plugins / routines, and does no version→CVE correlation on the version string it already parses. Wire-gap side: mysql.user rows, live PROCESSLIST client IPs, replication master/replica hosts, and @@version_compile_os are all captured or trivially available but never handed to the shared known_users / hostnames / relay_targets pools. Highest ROI adds are the caching_sha2/AuthSwitch pair (unblocks 8.0), mysql.func UDF check (immediate RCE detection), replication+slave_master_info+PROCESSLIST triple (topology + plaintext creds + client IPs), and version→CVE emit.
